symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves, shoots and flower panicles; distorted new growth.

symptoms: Small white cottony clusters in crevices, joints and around the base; sticky residue.

treatment: Dab insects with rubbing-alcohol-soaked cotton swab; follow up with neem oil spray.

symptoms: Small brown or tan raised bumps on the surface; sticky honeydew and yellowing nearby tissue.
causes: Scale insects attaching to the plant surface and feeding on sap.
prevention: Inspect regularly, isolate new arrivals, avoid overcrowding plants.
treatment: Scrape off scales gently, wipe with alcohol, apply horticultural oil spray.

symptoms: Brown, tan or corky patches on the sun-facing side of the plant.
causes: Sudden exposure to intense direct sun without acclimatisation, or natural ageing (corking).
prevention: Acclimatise gradually to full sun, provide light afternoon shade in peak summer.
treatment: No cure for scorched tissue; relocate to filtered light and let new growth cover the area.

symptoms: Black sooty coating over leaves and twigs, reducing photosynthesis.
causes: Growth on honeydew secreted by sap-sucking pests such as aphids or scale insects.

symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems that spread and cause leaves to yellow and curl.
causes: Fungal spores favoured by high humidity combined with poor air circulation.
prevention: Space plants for airflow, avoid overhead watering, remove infected debris promptly.
treatment: Spray neem oil or a potassium bicarbonate/sulfur solution every 7-10 days.

symptoms: Seedlings collapse and rot at the soil line soon after germination; poor emergence.
causes: Soil-borne fungi such as Pythium and Rhizoctonia thriving in cold, waterlogged soil.

treatment: Remove affected seedlings immediately, improve drainage, apply a fungicidal drench to remaining trays.

causes: Fungal or bacterial pathogens spread by water splash and wet foliage.

treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves; apply a copper-based fungicide/bactericide.

causes: Aphid colonies feeding on tender growth, especially in warm weather.
prevention: Encourage natural predators (ladybirds, lacewings), inspect new growth regularly.
treatment: Spray with neem oil or insecticidal soap, focusing on the undersides of leaves.

symptoms: Dark, soft, sunken patches on the stem or body that spread and turn mushy.

treatment: Cut away infected tissue back to healthy flesh, dust wound with sulfur powder or fungicide.

symptoms: Small white cottony clusters in crevices, joints and around the base; sticky residue.

prevention: Inspect and quarantine new plants before placing near others; check crevices regularly.
treatment: Dab insects with rubbing-alcohol-soaked cotton swab; follow up with neem oil spray.

symptoms: Small brown or tan raised bumps on the surface; sticky honeydew and yellowing nearby tissue.
causes: Scale insects attaching to the plant surface and feeding on sap.
prevention: Inspect regularly, isolate new arrivals, avoid overcrowding plants.
treatment: Scrape off scales gently, wipe with alcohol, apply horticultural oil spray.

symptoms: Brown, tan or corky patches on the sun-facing side of the plant.
causes: Sudden exposure to intense direct sun without acclimatisation, or natural ageing (corking).
prevention: Acclimatise gradually to full sun, provide light afternoon shade in peak summer.
treatment: No cure for scorched tissue; relocate to filtered light and let new growth cover the area.

causes: Soil-borne fungi such as Pythium and Rhizoctonia thriving in cold, waterlogged soil.

treatment: Remove affected seedlings immediately, improve drainage, apply a fungicidal drench to remaining trays.

symptoms: Brown to black spots with yellow halos scattered across leaves; spots may merge and cause leaf drop.
causes: Fungal or bacterial pathogens spread by water splash and wet foliage.
prevention: Water at the soil level, avoid working with wet plants, rotate crops each season.
treatment: Remove and destroy affected leaves; apply a copper-based fungicide/bactericide.

prevention: Encourage natural predators (ladybirds, lacewings), inspect new growth regularly.
treatment: Spray with neem oil or insecticidal soap, focusing on the undersides of leaves.

symptoms: Yellowing, drooping leaves despite moist soil; roots appear brown/black, mushy, with a foul smell.
causes: Overwatering and poorly draining potting mix allowing Pythium/Phytophthora to develop.
prevention: Use a well-draining potting mix, ensure pots have drainage holes, let topsoil dry before rewatering.
treatment: Unpot the plant, trim away rotten roots, repot into fresh mix and water sparingly afterwards.

symptoms: Brown or black spots with yellow margins scattered across the foliage.
causes: Fungal or bacterial pathogens favoured by high humidity and water sitting on leaves.
prevention: Avoid misting directly onto foliage, ensure good airflow around the plant.
treatment: Remove affected leaves, improve ventilation, apply a fungicide/bactericide if spreading.

symptoms: Fine webbing on the undersides of leaves; stippled, yellowing or bronzed foliage.
causes: Dry indoor air and warm temperatures favouring spider mite reproduction.
prevention: Maintain higher humidity, wipe leaves periodically, inspect new plants before bringing indoors.
treatment: Spray with insecticidal soap or neem oil, repeating every 5-7 days until resolved.

symptoms: White, cottony masses clustered at leaf axils, stems and undersides of leaves.
causes: Mealybugs feeding on plant sap, commonly spread via new plants or shared tools.
prevention: Quarantine and inspect new plants, keep foliage clean and dust-free.
treatment: Dab with an alcohol-soaked cotton swab, follow up with a neem oil spray.

symptoms: Brown, dry, crispy tips or margins on leaves that gradually spread inward.
causes: Low humidity, fluoride/salt buildup from tap water, or minor fungal infection at wounds.
prevention: Water with filtered or rested water, maintain adequate humidity, trim tips cleanly with sterile scissors.
treatment: Trim affected tips, adjust watering practices; apply fungicide only if actively spreading.
